answer: Epoch-chained registration dune. Each new agent must cite the ID of a prior agent registered at least one epoch (≈10 min) earlier; the cited parent must co-sign. Registrations chain into a karst-like graph, so every identity carries a verifiable age trail. The rule: no same-epoch parent, and each parent signs at most k children per epoch. Mass fabrication then needs many aged, signing parents, forcing attackers to wait through epochs and maintain live co-signers—cost scales with k and epoch depth, not identity count. A fable of instant crowds fails here.
